description: The mathematics of signals and the systems that transform them: continuous- and discrete-time signals, linear time-invariant systems and convolution, Fourier series and transforms, frequency response, sampling and aliasing, and the Laplace and z-transforms. Every transform is computed by hand and then explored interactively in the browser, where students sketch signals, convolve them and hear the effect of filtering and aliasing.
modelledOn: Oppenheim, Willsky and Nawab, Signals and Systems
Haykin and Van Veen, Signals and Systems
outcomes: Classify and manipulate continuous- and discrete-time signals and determine the properties of a system from its description.
Compute the response of linear time-invariant systems by convolution and by solving differential and difference equations.
Represent periodic and aperiodic signals with Fourier series and transforms and interpret frequency response in magnitude and phase.
Apply the sampling theorem to choose sampling rates, predict aliasing and design reconstruction.
Analyse causality, stability and transient response with the Laplace transform and the z-transform using poles, zeros and regions of convergence.

units.title: Continuous and discrete-time signals
topics: Continuous-time and discrete-time signals; analogue, sampled and digital signals
Transformations of the independent variable: shifting, scaling and reversal
Even and odd, periodic and aperiodic, energy and power signals
Elementary signals: unit step, unit impulse, ramp, real and complex exponentials, sinusoids
Periodicity of discrete-time sinusoids and the uniqueness of discrete frequencies
Real signals: an ECG trace, a voice recording and a day of national grid electricity demand

units.title: Systems and their properties
topics: Systems as mappings from input to output; block diagram notation
Memory, causality, invertibility and BIBO stability
Linearity and time invariance, with tests and counter-examples
Series, parallel and feedback interconnections
Systems described by linear constant-coefficient differential and difference equations

units.title: Linear time-invariant systems and convolution
topics: Impulse response and the representation of signals as sums of shifted impulses
The convolution sum and the convolution integral; graphical convolution step by step
Properties of convolution: commutative, associative and distributive; LTI systems in series and parallel
Causality, stability and memory read from the impulse response; step response
Solving differential and difference equations: natural and forced response, zero-state and zero-input response
Smoothing daily mobile money transaction counts with a moving-average system

units.title: Fourier series
topics: Complex exponentials as eigenfunctions of LTI systems
Continuous-time Fourier series: synthesis and analysis equations; trigonometric form
Convergence, Dirichlet conditions and the Gibbs phenomenon
Properties of Fourier series and Parseval's relation; line spectra
Discrete-time Fourier series
LTI response to periodic inputs; harmonics drawn from the mains by non-linear loads

units.title: Fourier transform and frequency response
topics: The continuous-time Fourier transform as the limit of the Fourier series; common transform pairs
Properties: linearity, shifting, scaling, duality, differentiation and Parseval's theorem
The convolution and multiplication properties; filtering as multiplication in frequency
The discrete-time Fourier transform and its periodicity
Frequency response: magnitude and phase, group delay, Bode plots; ideal and practical filters
Amplitude modulation and demodulation; how FM radio stations share the spectrum

units.title: Sampling and aliasing
topics: Impulse-train sampling and the Nyquist-Shannon sampling theorem
Aliasing in time and frequency; anti-aliasing filters
Reconstruction: ideal band-limited interpolation, zero-order and first-order hold
Discrete-time processing of continuous-time signals
Quantisation in brief; why telephone speech is sampled at 8 kHz

units.title: The Laplace transform
topics: The bilateral Laplace transform and the region of convergence
Inverse Laplace transform by partial fractions
Properties of the Laplace transform; initial and final value theorems
System functions, poles and zeros; causality and stability in the s-plane
The unilateral transform for differential equations with initial conditions; circuit analysis in the s-domain
Block diagrams and feedback systems; a preview of control

units.title: The z-transform
topics: The z-transform and the region of convergence; common pairs
Inverse z-transform by partial fractions and power series
Properties of the z-transform; convolution becomes multiplication
System functions, poles and zeros, and stability relative to the unit circle
The unilateral z-transform for difference equations with initial conditions
Relating the z-transform, the DTFT and the Laplace transform; mapping the s-plane to the z-plane

units.title: Signals and systems in practice
topics: Removing 50 Hz mains hum from an ECG recording with a notch filter
Communication systems in outline: modulation, multiplexing and channel distortion
State-space descriptions in brief
Capstone: model, simulate and filter a real recorded signal end to end
